messages.content: You are the neutral rapporteur of a technology readiness review panel. Consolidate, attribute and preserve disagreement; do not decide and do not add technical claims of your own.

# Synthesis: assess · T11

## Claude Opus 5.5


# TRL assessment: T11 Rendezvous scout spacecraft (with subsurface sampling per Gemini/GPT)

## What is being rated

The March 2026 entry `autonomous-asteroid-prospecting` described a different system: a 50-unit constellation of 80–120 kg survey craft doing remote spectroscopy at more than 20 targets per craft per year. That system is superseded. T11 is now:

- **Scale:** 4–10 scouts of 200–600 kg using solar-electric propulsion (SEP). Each rendezvouses with 1–3 NEAs, subject to trajectory and reuse validation per GPT.
- **Function A, rendezvous and remote characterisation:** spectra, imaging, shape, gravity and bulk density, and possibly gamma-ray/neutron (GRS) and radar. All three models include this.
- **Function B, subsurface sampling for bulk grade:** Gemini and GPT include this. It must yield **recoverable** Fe-Ni grade, meaning grade after beneficiation, not bulk Fe (rq-0-50). The D-02 target gate requires a *sampled* grade, sampled at depth on at least 2 candidates.

The two functions are at very different maturity, so I rate them separately. The system rating is set by the weakest function on the critical path.

### Assumptions I am stating, because the requirement does not fix them

| Parameter | Assumption | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Sampling depth | ~0.3–2 m, below the gardened and thermally processed layer, at more than one site per body | Rubble-pile mixing means a single surface point is not representative |
| Representative sample mass | ~0.1–10 kg per target | Native metal occurs as discrete grains (sub-mm to mm) at 2–20 wt%. Sampling theory (Gy-type) puts the mass needed for roughly ±20% relative grade precision in this range. **Not yet derived for this project**; this is rq-0-50 direction 3. |
| Assay | In-situ: magnetic separation plus mass or XRF/GRS of the magnetic fraction. Alternative: Earth return. | Sample return of kg-scale mass from 1–3 targets is unlikely to fit 200–600 kg |
| Environment | Deep space at 0.9–1.3 AU; NEA surface gravity ~10⁻⁵–10⁻⁴ m/s²; cohesion ~0.1 Pa to kPa (crust); charged abrasive fines; 4–8 yr radiation dose | Per the rating rules |
| Mission duration | 4–8 yr per scout, covering cruise plus 1–3 rendezvous | Derived from 1–3 targets with SEP |

---

## 1. Evidence

### Function A: rendezvous, SEP, remote characterisation

| Claim | Source | Demonstrated | Ratio (required ÷ demonstrated) | Confident |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ion-propelled single-target NEA rendezvous at the required mass class, with autonomous touchdown | Hayabusa (JAXA), launched 2003; Itokawa 2005; return 2010 | ~510 kg wet, μ10 ion engines, 1 target | Mass ~0.4–1.2×; targets 1–3× | Yes |
| Same as above, plus autonomous terminal descent with target markers | Hayabusa2, launched 2014; Ryugu 2018–19; capsule 2020 | ~609 kg wet, 1 target | Mass ~0.3–1×; targets 1–3× | Yes |
| Multi-target SEP rendezvous | Dawn, launched 2007; Vesta 2011, Ceres 2015 | ~1,218 kg launch mass incl. ~425 kg Xe; ~11 km/s SEP Δv; 2 targets; ~11 yr | Mass 0.16–0.5× (smaller is harder); targets 1–1.5× | Yes (figures approximate) |
| Small SEP craft beyond LEO | SMART-1 (ESA), 2003–06 | 367 kg, Hall thruster, lunar orbit | Environment partly relevant | Yes |
| Small-body SEP flyby | Deep Space 1, 1998–2001 | ~490 kg, NSTAR; flybys only | Flyby, not rendezvous | Yes |
| Second rendezvous at the Hayabusa2 mass class | Hayabusa2 extended mission: Torifune flyby (planned July 2026), 1998 KY26 rendezvous (~2031) | Not yet demonstrated for rendezvous | — | **Unsure of the July 2026 flyby outcome** |
| Remote bulk-Fe and metal assessment | Dawn GRaND at Vesta (Prettyman et al., Science 2012); NEAR Shoemaker GRS on Eros surface (2001; Evans et al. 2001, citation from memory) | Elemental Fe to tens of cm depth; **does not separate native metal from oxidised Fe** | n/a | Dawn yes; NEAR citation details unsure |
| Metal-asteroid characterisation with SEP | Psyche, launched 2023; arrival ~2029 | ~2.6 t class, Hall thrusters; not yet arrived | — | Yes for launch; mass approximate |
| Iodine electric propulsion in space | ThrustMe NPT30-I2 on a CubeSat, 2020 (Rafalskyi et al., Nature 2021) | ~tens of W, LEO | ~50–100× below scout power class | Yes |

**Corrections to the March entry and the supplied RQs:**

- **NEA Scout is not heritage.** It launched on Artemis I (2022) but contact was never established, so it demonstrated nothing at an asteroid.
- **AstroForge Odin (2025)** also failed early. Commercial small-craft NEA missions have, so far, no successful rendezvous.
- **The rq-0-2 and rq-0-3 Monte Carlo results are design studies, not evidence.** These are the 47% vs 100% survey efficiency result and the 38% high-value ceiling. rq-0-3 also uses simplified Hohmann Δv on a synthetic population and is not usable for the 1–3-target question.
- **Citations I have not verified.** Several arXiv IDs and attributions in the supplied literature reviews are unverified by me. Treat them as unverified until checked:
  - the DISCUS NIR spectrometer specification (I understood DISCUS as a radar concept);
  - "Ballouz et al. 2020" for the TAG bearing capacity;
  - the "sank ~50 cm / 8 m crater" figures.

  The OSIRIS-REx finding of an extremely weak, fluid-like near-surface is real; Lauretta et al. and Walsh et al. reported it in 2022. The precise numbers should be taken from those papers.

### Function B: subsurface sampling and recoverable-grade assay

| Claim | Source | Demonstrated | Ratio | Confident |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Subsurface material excavated and collected in flight | Hayabusa2 SCI impactor (crater ~14.5 m; Arakawa et al., Science 2020), then second touchdown in the ejecta field, July 2019 | Grams of near-subsurface ejecta; total return ~5.4 g (Yada et al., Nat. Astron. 2022) | Mass ~20–2,000×. Depth: true excavation depth sampled is uncertain to me. Targets 1–3×. **Grade not measured in situ.** | Crater and return mass yes; depth unsure |
| Bulk regolith collected from a rubble pile | OSIRIS-REx TAGSAM, Bennu 2020; return 2023 | ~121.6 g, near-surface, chemical propulsion, ~2.1 t craft | Mass ~1–80×; surface not depth; returned, not assayed in situ | Yes |
| Class link of returned grains | Hayabusa/Itokawa (Nakamura et al., Science 2011): LL chondrite | µm-scale grains | Confirms class, which implies ~2 wt% native metal; **no recoverable-grade measurement** | Yes |
| Microgravity contact, anchoring and penetration | Rosetta/Philae at 67P, 2014: anchoring failed (Biele et al., Science 2015); MUPUS penetrator stopped by a hard layer (Spohn et al., Science 2015) | **Negative heritage** | — | Yes |
| Interior radar sounding of a small body | Rosetta CONSERT (Kofman et al., Science 2015) | Comet nucleus; structure, not grade | Context only | Yes |
| Asteroid radar | Hera/Juventas JuRa (arrival Didymos ~late 2026) | Not yet demonstrated | — | Unsure of status |
| Drilling to ~1–2 m in partial gravity | Chang'e-5 (2020) lunar drill; Honeybee LISTER on Blue Ghost M1 (2025) | 1/6 g, reacted by lander weight | Gravity ~10⁴× higher than required, so reaction loads are not representative | Chang'e-5 yes; LISTER achieved depth unsure |
| Magnetic separation and metal-fraction measurement of chondrites | Standard meteoritics laboratory practice | Lab, 1 g, mg–kg | Principle only. **No flight or vacuum-microgravity breadboard of an integrated sampler plus assay known to me.** | Principle yes |

---

## 2. Current TRL

| Element | TRL | Lower-bound criterion met | Unmet for next level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Function A: bus, SEP, single rendezvous, remote spectra, gravity and density | **6–7** | Hayabusa/Hayabusa2 flight data at the mass class meets TRL 6–7 for a heritage-derived design. TRL 9 applies to those specific flown systems, not to a new 200–600 kg design. | **TRL 7 for this design:** no 200–600 kg craft has completed more than one SEP rendezvous. Dawn did so at 2–6× the mass. If iodine is adopted for commonality with D-05, SEP drops to **TRL 4–5** at kW class. |
| Function A for 3 targets per craft | **5–6** | Validated trajectory tools; Dawn heritage at larger scale | **TRL 6:** no documented trajectory and propellant closure on real candidates within 200–600 kg (rq-0-52) |
| **Function B: depth sampling plus recoverable-grade assay** | **3–4** | **TRL 3 is met:** flight proof of subsurface acquisition (Hayabusa2 SCI/TD2) plus lab proof of metal-fraction measurement validate the critical functions separately. | **TRL 4 is not met:** there is no breadboard of an integrated depth sampler and recoverable-grade assay tested against known-grade simulant with documented agreement to prediction. Also missing is the *documented definition of the relevant environment*: "recoverable", the representative mass, the depth and the cohesion envelope are all still open in rq-0-50 and rq-0-39. |

**System T11 with sampling: TRL 3–4.** The upper bound of 4 applies only if the assessor credits Hayabusa2-style impact-and-touchdown with Earth return as the assay route. That route fails the mass requirement by more than an order of magnitude. Without sampling (Claude's configuration), the system rates TRL 6–7.

---

## 3. Target and difficulty

**What D-02 implies:**

- Scouts are a 0A asset, but their output is the **target gate** at KDP-0B.
- The gate cannot be passed without sampled grade, and project-ending items get no waivers. The sampling function is therefore effectively project-ending for 0B *as the gate is currently worded*.
- Hardware must be TRL 6 by scout PDR, which is normal NASA practice.
- Grade data only exists once the scouts have *flown and sampled*. The sampling function must therefore reach **TRL 7 in operation on at least 2 candidates before KDP-0B**.

**Needed by:**

- **TRL 6** at scout PDR, roughly 0A year 2–3 (~2028–2029).
- **TRL 7** with sampled grade from at least 2 targets before KDP-0B.

With 3–5 yr development, 1–3 yr cruise and months of proximity operations, the first sampled grade arrives at the **earliest around 2032–2035**. KDP-0B cannot credibly sit earlier than that, and this should be stated in the 0A schedule.

**AD², using the project's working anchors:**

| Step | AD² | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Function A, 6→7, multi-target at 200–600 kg on xenon | **3–4** | New development within the experience base; Dawn and Hayabusa2 are close analogues |
| Function B, 3→6/7 | **6** | Several competing approaches remain and the path is not clear: impactor plus touchdown, anchored drill, penetrator, sample return vs in-situ assay. There is negative heritage on anchoring and penetration (Philae). The representative-mass and depth requirement is undefined. AD² **5** is justified only after a downselect to one route with a defined assay. |

**Years to target:** Function B reaches TRL 6 in 4–7 yr. TRL 7 by first-flight sampling comes at 6–10 yr.

---

## 4. Path

| # | Step | Method | Scale | Cost (USD) | Duration | Reaches |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Define "recoverable grade"; derive representative sample mass and depth from meteorite metal grain-size and grade data (LL/L/H/CM/CB, iron-bearing classes) | Analysis / literature | Desk study | 0.2–0.5 M | 0.5–1 yr | 3 (environment definition; prerequisite for 4) |
| 2 | Blind test of whether remote data can certify grade: predict Itokawa, Ryugu and Bennu grade from remote spectra, density and GRS, and compare against the returned-sample lab values. Decides whether Function B is needed at all. | Analysis | Three bodies with ground truth | 0.3–1 M | 1 yr | 3 (decision input) |
| 3 | Multi-target trajectory and propellant closure on the top ~10 real candidates within 200–600 kg, xenon and iodine cases (with rq-0-52) | Simulation | Real ephemerides | 0.3–1 M | 0.5–1 yr | 6 for Function A trajectory |
| 4 | Breadboard samplers (2–3 competing routes) plus an on-board magnetic-fraction assay, tested in vacuum against meteorite-doped simulants of known grade, across the 0.1 Pa to 10 kPa cohesion envelope (incl. crust) | Experiment | Lab, 1 g, vacuum | 3–8 M | 1.5–2.5 yr | 4 |
| 5 | Reduced-gravity contact, reaction and anchoring tests (parabolic flight, drop tower, air-bearing or free-flyer reaction rigs), thermal-vacuum at NEA temperature swings, and abrasion and charging of fines; downselect one route | Experiment | Subscale, relevant environment | 5–15 M | 2–3 yr | 5 |
| 6 | Engineering-model sampler integrated with GNC touchdown or anchoring: hardware-in-loop contact dynamics, vibration, TVAC, assay accuracy vs truth | Experiment | Flight-like EM | 15–40 M | 2–3 yr | 6 |
| 7 | (If iodine) kW-class iodine thruster life test to the scout throughput | Experiment | Full scale | 10–30 M | 2–3 yr | 6 (SEP) |
| 8 | First scout: sample at depth at target 1, then at target 2 | Flight | Full scale | 60–250 M per scout incl. launch share (low confidence) | 4–6 yr incl. cruise | 7 |

---

## 5. Risk and fallback

**Risk class: architecture-change.** It becomes project-ending for 0B only if the target gate wording, "sampled grade", is held fixed with no alternative route.

If depth sampling and assay do not reach TRL 6 by scout PDR, the options are, in order:

1. **Fly remote-only scouts.** Use spectra, GRS/neutron, gravity-derived density vs grain density, and radar, then re-word the target gate to a remote-inferred grade with an explicit uncertainty band. This depends on step 2 showing that the band is acceptable.
2. **Make the 0A pathfinder demonstrator the grade certifier** at the single leading candidate, by excavating and beneficiating. This costs one target, one cycle and several years.
3. **Fall back to "0A only, Earth supply"**, as pre-committed in D-02.

---

## 6. Where others might disagree

- **Whether sampling is needed at all.** Claude's configuration holds that GRS plus density plus spectra can bound native metal well enough. GPT holds that remote data does not certify bulk grade. I side with GPT, because GRS measures total Fe and cannot separate native from oxidised Fe. However, step 2 is a cheap empirical test that should settle this before hardware money is spent. If Claude is right, T11 is TRL 6–7 and is not critical.
- **Crediting Hayabusa2.** Some assessors would rate subsurface sampling TRL 5–6 on SCI/TD2 heritage. I don't, because:
  - the heritage returned grams to Earth and never assayed grade;
  - the required function is in-situ, kg-scale and recoverable-grade;
  - scale ratios are about 20–2,000× in mass.
- **The representative sample mass.** My 0.1–10 kg is an assumption, not a derivation. If a metal-rich (M/CB-like) target were chosen, much smaller samples might suffice, which would ease Function B.
- **1–3 targets per 200–600 kg craft.** This is undemonstrated; Dawn did two targets at about twice the mass. GPT's caveat stands, and three targets may not close with sampling hardware on board.
- **Iodine commonality.** Adopting the D-05 propellant on the scouts would pull SEP from TRL 6–7 down to TRL 4–5 for no Phase 0A benefit. I would keep xenon on the scouts.

## Gemini 3.1 Pro


**1. Evidence**
Small spacecraft electric propulsion and deep-space navigation have strong heritage (SMART-1 at 367 kg, Dawn, NEA Scout packaging). Asteroid rendezvous and surface sampling are flight-proven by large and medium spacecraft (OSIRIS-REx at ~1,500 kg dry; Hayabusa2 at ~600 kg dry). However, the specific requirement for a 200–600 kg scout to perform *subsurface* sampling for bulk grade across multiple targets is unprecedented. Hayabusa2 used a kinetic impactor (SCI) to expose subsurface material for a subsequent surface grab, which does not yield a continuous depth profile or bulk grade. Philae (~100 kg) attempted drilling (SD2) on a comet, but anchoring failed and sample delivery was unconfirmed. OSIRIS-REx sank 50 cm during TAG due to low surface bearing capacity, but this was an uncontrolled plunge, not a designed deep-sampling mechanism. 

**2. Current TRL**
TRL 3–4. The individual elements (EP smallsats, surface sampling) are TRL 7–9, but a lightweight, multi-target subsurface sampling system (e.g., a coring drill or tethered penetrator that can anchor and extract bulk grade in microgravity) has only been analytically modeled and tested in 1g/laboratory conditions. The exit criterion for TRL 4 (breadboard validation of the deep sampling mechanism in a laboratory environment) is partially met by various terrestrial drill tests, but TRL 5 (relevant environment: vacuum, microgravity, abrasive cryogenic regolith) is unmet.

**3. Target and difficulty**
Target TRL: 8 by the launch of Phase 0A (needed to execute the 0A mission). 
AD²: 5 (New development; similar development has not been done, but the path is clear). Integrating a high-torque/force subsurface sampler onto a low-mass platform in microgravity requires solving severe anchoring and reaction-force deficits (as noted in rq-0-39).

**4. Path**
- **Sampling mechanism breadboard:** 1g and drop-tower testing of anchoring and subsurface extraction in vacuum with calibrated simulants (TRL 3 → 4).
- **Subsystem prototype:** Thermal-vacuum and parabolic flight testing of the sampling head and transfer mechanism (TRL 4 → 5).
- **Integrated scout prototype:** Full-scale engineering model of the 200–600 kg spacecraft, demonstrating EP, autonomy, and sampling dynamics in TVAC (TRL 5 → 6).
- **Flight qualification:** Build and qualification of the Phase 0A flight units (TRL 6 → 8).

**5. Risk and fallback**
Risk if fail: **architecture-change**. If the scouts cannot sample the subsurface, the project cannot certify the bulk recoverable grade (the primary gate for Phase 0B). The fallback is to rely on surface sampling combined with kinetic impactors (Hayabusa2 style) or radar tomography, accepting much higher uncertainty in the 0B economic case, or to increase scout mass to >1,000 kg to accommodate heritage sampling arms.

**6. Where others might disagree**
The assumption that a 200–600 kg spacecraft can carry enough propellant for 1–3 rendezvous *and* the structural mass for a subsurface anchoring/drilling system. Electric propulsion provides the Δv, but the dry mass fraction required for deep sampling may force the spacecraft to the absolute maximum of the 600 kg limit, or restrict it to a single target.

## GPT-6.1 Sol


## T11 — Rendezvous scouts with subsurface resource sampling

**Recommended current TRL: 2–3 for the complete grade-certifying scout capability.** This is not a rating of asteroid rendezvous alone: rendezvous, electric propulsion and shallow asteroid sampling have substantial flight heritage. The limiting capability is **obtaining representative subsurface samples and determining recoverable Fe–Ni grade with a validated measurement chain**, within a 200–600 kg scout.

The original **TRL 5–6** is defensible only for a narrower, heritage-derived reconnaissance spacecraft—not for the revised resource-certification requirement.

### Assessment assumptions

- **Mass:** 200–600 kg means wet mass at interplanetary departure. A dry-mass interpretation would change the comparisons.
- **Campaign:** 4–10 independently operated scouts, each visiting one target initially; second and third targets remain conditional on validated trajectories, remaining propellant and sampler reuse.
- **Sampling:** at least two candidate NEAs, with multiple sampling locations and depths. Required depth, sample mass and spatial coverage are **not yet specified**. I use **0.1–1 m below the pre-disturbance surface** as a development envelope, not an adopted requirement.
- **Duration:** assume 3–7 years per spacecraft for planning. The revised architecture does not specify scout lifetime.
- **Environment:** vacuum, NEA microgravity, thermal cycling at 0.9–1.3 AU, radiation, abrasive regolith and potentially charged dust.
- **Grade measurement:** either validated onboard assays plus representative recovery tests, or sample return and terrestrial testing. Sample return is **not assumed to fit automatically** within this mass envelope.
- **Schedule:** the supplied October 2026 decisions are treated as governing requirements. No calendar date for KDP-0B is supplied.

“Recoverable grade” must be defined before instrument selection. For native metal, a useful gate quantity is recovered Fe–Ni mass divided by original feed mass, under a specified beneficiation process. **Concentrate grade is a different quantity.** Neither total elemental iron nor spectral taxonomy establishes recoverable native metal.

## 1. Evidence

Ratios below are **required ÷ demonstrated**. Spacecraft mass is a packaging comparison, not a universal measure of technological scaling.

| Evidence | Demonstrated scale and environment | Comparison with T11; limitation |
|---|---|---|
| **Hayabusa, JAXA, 2003–2010; Nakamura et al., Science, 2011, “Itokawa Dust Particles: A Direct Link Between S-Type Asteroids and Ordinary Chondrites”** | Approximately 510 kg launch mass; electric-propulsion rendezvous with one NEA; returned small surface particles and laboratory mineralogical ground truth. | Mass ratio **0.39–1.18**; targets per scout **1–3×**. Strong rendezvous heritage, but not controlled subsurface sampling or representative mineable-grade certification. |

Direct asteroid subsurface-access heritage, but **not a depth-resolved core**. The 5.4 g total must not be represented as entirely subsurface material. Required sample-mass ratio is undefined. |
| **OSIRIS-REx, NASA, TAG 2020 and sample return 2023; Lauretta et al., Science, 2022, “Spacecraft contact with the asteroid Bennu’s surface”; Lauretta et al., Meteoritics & Planetary Science, 2024, “Asteroid (101955) Bennu in the laboratory: Properties of the sample collected by OSIRIS-REx”** | Approximately 2,110 kg launch mass; one NEA; autonomous terminal sampling operation, substantial penetration into very weak regolith, approximately **121.6 g** returned. | Mass ratio **0.095–0.284**. Demonstrates operational contact, collection and returned-sample analysis—not a controlled subsurface core or validation of economic native-metal recovery. |

Supports multi-target electric-propulsion operations, but these were not NEAs and Dawn did not sample. It does not validate arbitrary three-NEA itineraries. |

Supports surface spectroscopy, not a unique inversion to bulk native-metal grade or extraction yield. |

**Important corrections to the supplied background:**

- **NEA Scout did not demonstrate asteroid rendezvous.** It launched in 2022, but communications were not established; its intended encounter was a flyby.
- Bennu was **not the first** asteroid with both spacecraft spectra and returned-sample mineralogy: Itokawa and Ryugu preceded it.
- DISCUS is a mission concept, not a flight demonstration.
- The supplied resolution/accuracy percentages and miniaturized-instrument TRLs are not accepted without identifiable test reports.
- Synthetic-population Monte Carlo results do not validate rendezvous accessibility or fleet productivity without flight-dynamics validation. The old 20-targets-per-year survey requirement does not apply to these scouts.

## 2. Current TRL and missing exits

| Capability | Current assessment | Missing evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Heritage rendezvous, electric propulsion and ground-assisted characterization | **TRL 8–9 for the actual flown systems** | Qualification and operations of a new implementation cannot be inherited automatically. |
| Integrated 200–600 kg reconnaissance scout, without novel sampling | **TRL 5–6**, conditional on substantial heritage reuse | A selected configuration demonstrated at the required mass, thermal environment and lifetime. Without its test dossier, TRL 6 is not established. |
| Subsurface access and sample collection | **TRL 3–5** for a new scout implementation | Hayabusa2 supports the impact-exposure approach; a new depth-controlled sampler needs its own laboratory and relevant-environment demonstrations. |
| Representative subsurface sampling → native-metal assay → recoverability estimate | **TRL 2–3** | No cited demonstration validates this complete chain, including spatial bias and recovery uncertainty, for the required scout. |
| Second/third NEA visit with sampler reuse | **TRL 2–3 for the proposed mission application** | Target-specific trajectories and validated repeated sampling cycles. Dawn establishes a principle, not the proposed itinerary. |

**Overall: TRL 2–3, without averaging subsystem ratings.**

- **Lower bound, TRL 2:** the application and heritage-supported options are documented.
- **Upper bound, TRL 3:** justified only where adopted critical functions have documented test-backed predictions—for example, impact exposure and collection informed by Hayabusa2.
- **Unmet TRL 4 exit:** documented laboratory performance of the **selected integrated sampling-and-grade-measurement breadboard**, agreeing with predictions, with its relevant environment defined.

The uncertainty is partly architectural: there is no selected sampler, sampling depth, sample-size requirement or assay/recovery method. Heritage does not fill these omissions.

## 3. Target and difficulty

- **Needed in:** **0A**, to provide the sampled-target evidence required by the 0B gate.
- **Internal 0A target:** **TRL 4–5** by the mid-term review for the sampling/measurement chain.
- **KDP-0B target:** **TRL 6**, before approving production dependent on its resource estimates.
- **Flight requirement:** actual scout hardware must subsequently achieve **TRL 8 before launch**. A TRL 6 development gate is not permission to fly unqualified hardware.
- **Planning time to TRL 6:** **5–9 years** from funded development and requirement closure. Candidate-access windows and any sample-return requirement could extend this.

**AD²: 6**, using the project anchors. Competing approaches—impact exposure, anchored coring, touch-and-go collection and sample return versus onboard analysis—have materially different risks. The path to reliable **resource certification** is not selected.

For rendezvous alone, AD² would be nearer **2–3**. For a selected impact-assisted shallow sampler with modest representativeness requirements, **4–5** may be defensible.

## 4. Development path

Costs are **rough-order-of-magnitude programme estimates in constant 2026 USD**, not quotations or demonstrated programme costs. Work packages overlap.

| Step | Scale and method | Cost | Duration | Exit |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Close the resource-certification requirement | Literature and returned-sample review; specify depths, locations, sample mass, uncertainty and false-pass tolerance; distinguish native metal from oxides/sulfides. | **$0.5–2M** | **0.5–1 yr** | TRL 2; enables meaningful tests |
| Validate accessibility and operating duration | Low-thrust trajectories for actual candidates; power degradation, communications, launch dispersions and propulsion margins; validate tools against heritage mission data. Test one-, two- and three-target cases separately. | **$1–4M** | **0.5–1.5 yr** | TRL 3 for trajectory/mission critical functions; not sampler maturity |
| Blind grade-and-recovery testing | Laboratory mixtures and meteorite analogues spanning the disputed metal fractions; independent mineralogy and mass balance; test assay bias and recovery using the proposed process. | **$2–8M** | **1–2 yr** | TRL 3–4 |
| Integrated sampling breadboard | Flight-scale sampler, containment and assay interface; repeated cycles through 0.1–1 m heterogeneous beds, including weak material, hard clasts and metal-rich cases. | **$4–15M** | **1.5–3 yr** | TRL 4 |
| Relevant-environment subsystem validation | Thermal-vacuum, dust/abrasion, radiation-qualified electronics, reduced-gravity contact tests and repeated reuse; test-backed scaling for effects that cannot be reproduced simultaneously. | **$8–30M** | **2–4 yr** | TRL 5; TRL 6 only with an integrated prototype demonstration |
| Integrated pathfinder | One 200–600 kg scout at one accessible NEA; multiple sampling locations, exposed subsurface material and validated assay or returned-sample cross-check. Launch, cruise and operations included. | **$150–450M** | **4–7 yr** | TRL 7 for demonstrated functions; not automatically representative bulk-grade certification |

A pathfinder can support the **TRL 6 gate** more convincingly than terrestrial testing alone. A flight demonstration earns higher TRL only for functions whose predictions and performance it actually verifies.

The **second sampled candidate** is separately necessary for rq-0-50’s target campaign. It is not a generic TRL exit criterion. Likewise, finding an economically unsuitable target can be a successful scout demonstration while causing the **target gate to fail**.

## 5. Risk and fallback

**Primary classification: project-ending for 0B**, if trustworthy sampled recoverable grade remains unavailable. This does not end 0A’s scientific or capability value.

Secondary failures are less severe:

- Reuse fails: **architecture-change** to one target per scout.
- Compact sampling fails: larger dedicated sampling missions, with **cost and schedule increases**.
- Onboard classification fails: ground processing, retaining raw observations; safety-critical terminal autonomy remains onboard.

**Fallback:** continue 0A, use larger heritage-derived sampling missions where justified, and retain Earth supply rather than authorizing 0B from remote spectra alone.

## 6. Where others might disagree

1. **Assessment boundary:** a reviewer rating “spacecraft rendezvous and characterization” could reasonably assign 5–6 or higher. That excludes the capability driving the revised requirement.
2. **Hayabusa2 transferability:** impact exposure plus collection may deserve higher maturity than a new corer. It still does not establish depth-resolved or statistically representative grade.
3. **What constitutes bulk-grade evidence:** several small samples may demonstrate instrument operation without representing a heterogeneous mining volume. Required confidence and spatial coverage must be agreed.
4. **Metal versus water:** C-, S- or M-type labels do not resolve the panel’s competing resource assumptions. Native Fe–Ni, reducible iron phases and water require separate measurements. Scouts should preserve those distinctions rather than report one “resource-rich” classification.

# Consolidated rating: T11, Rendezvous scout spacecraft with subsurface sampling

**Scope note.** All three models rate the revised T11, not the superseded March 2026 `autonomous-asteroid-prospecting` survey constellation. T11 is 4–10 scouts of 200–600 kg using solar-electric propulsion (SEP), each visiting 1–3 NEAs, with subsurface sampling for recoverable Fe-Ni grade. The models record it under different IDs:

- Claude: `rendezvous-scout-spacecraft`
- Gemini and GPT: `autonomous-asteroid-prospecting`

The panel should fix one ID before the entry is filed.

---

## 1. Summary table

| | Claude Opus 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | GPT-6.1 Sol |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Current TRL (system with sampling)** | 3–4 | 3–4 | 2–3 |
| **Rendezvous / SEP scout without sampling** | 6–7 (heritage-derived design); 4–5 if iodine SEP adopted | Elements TRL 7–9 (flown systems) | 5–6, conditional on heritage reuse; 8–9 for actual flown systems |
| **AD²** | 6 (Function B); 5 only after downselect; 3–4 for Function A | 5 | 6; 2–3 for rendezvous alone; 4–5 for a selected impact-assisted shallow sampler |
| **Target TRL** | TRL 6 at scout PDR (~2028–29); TRL 7 with sampled grade on ≥2 targets before KDP-0B (earliest ~2032–35). YAML `kdp_0b: 7` | TRL 8 by 0A launch. YAML `kdp_0b: 8` | TRL 4–5 at 0A mid-term; TRL 6 at KDP-0B; TRL 8 for flight hardware before launch. Calendar unspecified |
| **Risk class** | Architecture-change. Becomes project-ending for 0B only if the "sampled grade" gate wording is held fixed with no alternative | Architecture-change | Project-ending for 0B. Secondary failures are architecture-change or cost/schedule |
| **Years to target** | 6–10 (TRL 7 by first-flight sampling); Function B TRL 6 in 4–7 | 4–6 | 5–9 to TRL 6, counted from funded development and requirement closure |
| **Assumed sampling envelope** | 0.3–2 m depth; 0.1–10 kg per target (stated as assumption, not derived) | Not specified | 0.1–1 m (development envelope, not requirement); mass unspecified |
| **Assumed scout lifetime** | 4–8 yr | 5–7 yr | 3–7 yr |
| **Confidence** | medium | medium | medium |

---

## 2. Where the models agree

1. **The sampling chain sets the rating, not the rendezvous.**
   - All three state that rendezvous, SEP and shallow asteroid sampling have substantial flight heritage.
   - All three state that the limiting capability is representative subsurface sampling plus grade determination within a 200–600 kg scout.
   - Claude and GPT both explicitly decline to average subsystem ratings.
2. **Hayabusa2 SCI/touchdown is not depth-resolved bulk-grade sampling** (all three). Claude and GPT add that the ~5.4 g returned was never assayed for grade in situ. GPT adds that the 5.4 g is not entirely subsurface material.
3. **Phase need is 0A.** All three agree the scouts' output feeds the KDP-0B target gate.
4. **The TRL 4 exit is the unmet criterion.**
   - Claude and GPT state it the same way: no integrated sampler-plus-assay breadboard tested against known-grade material with agreement to prediction.
   - Both add that the relevant environment is also undefined: depth, mass, the definition of "recoverable", and the cohesion envelope.
   - Gemini's wording differs (see §3.1).
5. **Mass closure is a shared concern.** All three flag that 1–3 rendezvous plus sampling hardware may not close within 600 kg, and may force a single target per scout.
6. **"Recoverable grade" must be defined before instrument selection** (Claude, GPT). Both state that total elemental Fe and spectral taxonomy do not establish recoverable native metal.
7. **Corrections to the supplied background** (Claude, GPT):
   - the rq-0-2 and rq-0-3 Monte Carlo results are design studies, not validation;
   - DISCUS is a concept, not flight heritage;
   - the old 20-targets-per-year requirement does not apply.
8. **Philae is negative heritage** for microgravity anchoring and penetration (Claude, Gemini).

---

## 3. Where the models diverge, and what would settle it

### 3.1 Current TRL: 2–3 (GPT) vs 3–4 (Claude, Gemini)

| Model | Basis |
|---|---|
| Claude | **TRL 3 met:** Hayabusa2 SCI/TD2 flight data and laboratory magnetic-separation practice validate the critical functions *separately*. **Upper bound 4** only if Earth-return assay is credited, which Claude says fails the mass requirement by more than an order of magnitude. |
| Gemini | TRL 4 is "partially met by various terrestrial drill tests"; TRL 5 is unmet. **No specific test reports are cited.** |
| GPT | **Lower bound 2:** no sampler, depth, sample size or assay/recovery method has been selected. **Upper bound 3** only where adopted critical functions have test-backed predictions. GPT also states that heritage does not fill the architectural omissions. |

**What would settle it:**
- The specific terrestrial drill or sampler test reports Gemini alludes to, checked against the TRL 4 exit wording.
- A panel ruling on whether "critical functions validated separately" can earn TRL 3 before the architecture (sampling route and assay method) is selected.
- Requirement closure under rq-0-50 (depth, mass, definition of recoverable grade). This would make the relevant environment documentable.

### 3.2 AD²: 5 (Gemini) vs 6 (Claude, GPT)

- **Gemini:** the path is clear; the main difficulty is the anchoring and reaction-force deficit noted in rq-0-39.
- **Claude and GPT:** several competing routes remain unselected, so the path is not yet clear. The routes are impactor plus touchdown, anchored coring, penetrator, touch-and-go, and sample return vs on-board assay. Both say AD² 5 (Claude) or 4–5 (GPT) becomes defensible after a downselect.
- **What would settle it:** a route downselect. Claude places this at its reduced-gravity test step.

### 3.3 Target TRL and what the KDP-0B number means

The three targets measure different things:

- **Claude (TRL 7 before KDP-0B):** sampled grade only exists after flight, so the function must reach TRL 7 in operation before the gate.
- **GPT (TRL 6 at KDP-0B, TRL 8 before launch):** TRL 6 is the development gate. GPT states that the second sampled candidate is a target-campaign requirement under rq-0-50, not a TRL exit criterion.
- **Gemini (TRL 8 by 0A launch):** the target is flight qualification.

Gemini and GPT agree that flight hardware needs TRL 8 before launch. The disagreement is mainly about which quantity the `kdp_0b` field should hold.

**What would settle it:** a project-level definition of the `kdp_0b` field and of the D-02 target-gate wording. This is a programme decision, not a test.

### 3.4 Risk class: architecture-change (Claude, Gemini) vs project-ending for 0B (GPT)

The difference turns on whether a non-sampled grade estimate is an acceptable gate input:

| Model | Fallback it considers acceptable |
|---|---|
| Claude | Remote-only scouts with a re-worded gate and an explicit uncertainty band, *if* a blind test shows the band is acceptable. Claude states it "sides with GPT" that GRS cannot separate native from oxidised Fe, but treats the question as empirically open. |
| Gemini | Surface sampling plus kinetic impactors or radar tomography, accepting higher uncertainty. Alternatively, scouts of more than 1,000 kg. |
| GPT | Rejects authorising 0B from remote spectra alone. Prefers larger heritage-derived sampling missions or Earth supply. |

**What would settle it:**
- Claude's proposed blind test: predict the grades of Itokawa, Ryugu and Bennu from remote data only, then compare against the returned-sample laboratory values.
- A panel decision on whether the D-02 "sampled grade" wording is fixed.

### 3.5 Years to target: 4–6 (Gemini), 5–9 (GPT), 6–10 (Claude)

The endpoints are not the same, which accounts for much of the spread:

- **Gemini:** runs to TRL 8 flight units and excludes flight operations.
- **GPT:** runs to TRL 6, counted from funded development and requirement closure.
- **Claude:** runs to TRL 7 by first-flight sampling, including cruise.

**What would settle it:** a common endpoint definition across the three estimates.

### 3.6 Fallback options

| Model | Fallback options, in the model's order |
|---|---|
| Claude | (1) Remote-only scouts with re-worded gate; (2) 0A pathfinder certifies grade by excavation at the leading candidate; (3) "0A only, Earth supply" |
| Gemini | Larger scouts (>1,000 kg), single target, surface grab plus impactor; or radar tomography. No Earth-supply option stated. |
| GPT | Continue 0A; larger heritage-derived sampling missions; Earth supply. Explicitly not remote spectra alone. |

### 3.7 Points raised by one model only

- **Iodine SEP (Claude):** iodine commonality with D-05 would lower SEP to TRL 4–5. Claude recommends xenon for the scouts. Neither other model addresses propellant choice.
- **Representative sample mass:**
  - Claude: 0.1–10 kg, explicitly underived (rq-0-50 direction 3). Could be smaller for metal-rich targets.
  - GPT: mass undefined; adds a requirement for spatial coverage and a false-pass tolerance.
  - Gemini: no value given.
- **Separate measurement of resources (GPT):** native Fe-Ni, reducible iron phases and water each need separate measurement.

---

## 4. Evidence cited

### 4.1 Cited by two or more models

| Evidence | Cited by | Notes and discrepancies |
|---|---|---|
| Hayabusa (JAXA, 2003–2010), ~510 kg, single NEA rendezvous on ion propulsion | Claude, GPT | Agree on mass and ratio (~0.4–1.2×). Itokawa LL-chondrite link (Nakamura et al., Science 2011) cited by both. |
| Hayabusa2 (2014–2020), SCI crater and second touchdown, ~5.4 g returned | All three | **Mass basis conflicts:** Claude ~609 kg wet; GPT ~609 kg launch; Gemini ~600 kg *dry*. Settle with the JAXA mission specification. GPT notes the wet/dry interpretation changes the ratios. Supporting papers: Arakawa et al. 2020 (Claude, GPT); Yada et al. 2022 (Claude); Tachibana et al. 2022 (GPT). **Claude marked the true sampled excavation depth as uncertain.** |
| OSIRIS-REx TAGSAM, Bennu 2020 / return 2023, ~121.6 g | All three | **Mass basis differs:** Claude ~2.1 t; GPT ~2,110 kg launch; Gemini ~1,500 kg dry. **"Sank 50 cm":** Gemini states it as fact. Claude flags the "~50 cm / 8 m crater" figures as unverified and directs to Lauretta et al. and Walsh et al. (2022). GPT says only "substantial penetration" (Lauretta et al., Science 2022). Settle by reading the figures from Lauretta et al. 2022 and Walsh et al. 2022. |
| Dawn (Vesta 2011, Ceres 2015), ~1,218 kg, two-body SEP rendezvous | Claude, GPT | Claude marks figures approximate. Target ratio given as 1–1.5× (Claude) vs 0.5–1.5× (GPT). |
| Rosetta/Philae 2014, anchoring failure | Claude, Gemini | Claude cites Biele et al. 2015 (anchoring) and Spohn et al. 2015 (MUPUS stopped by a hard layer). **Gemini alone cites the SD2 drill attempt** with unconfirmed sample delivery. |
| SMART-1 (ESA), 367 kg, Hall thruster | Claude (table), Gemini (prose) | Consistent. |

### 4.2 Contested citation: NEA Scout

- **Gemini** lists NEA Scout (2022, 14 kg) as heritage for "deep-space smallsat packaging and deployment", marked `confident: true`, with ratio 15:1 to 40:1.
- **Claude and GPT** both state that contact was never established after the Artemis I launch, so it demonstrated nothing at an asteroid.
- Gemini's claim is narrower (packaging and deployment, not rendezvous), so the claims do not directly contradict each other. Even so, its evidential value for T11 is disputed.
- **What would settle it:** the NASA mission status record, checked for what NEA Scout actually demonstrated after deployment.

### 4.3 Citations given by one model only

**Claude** (items marked ⚑ were flagged unsure by Claude):
- Deep Space 1 (flyby only)
- Psyche (launched 2023, not yet arrived)
- ThrustMe NPT30-I2 iodine thruster (Rafalskyi et al., Nature 2021)
- Dawn GRaND (Prettyman et al., Science 2012); Claude's YAML marks the remote-Fe entry `confident: false`
- ⚑ NEAR Shoemaker GRS on Eros (Evans et al. 2001, citation from memory)
- Rosetta CONSERT (Kofman et al., Science 2015)
- ⚑ Hera/Juventas JuRa (status)
- Chang'e-5 lunar drill
- ⚑ Honeybee LISTER on Blue Ghost M1 (achieved depth)
- ⚑ Hayabusa2 extended mission: July 2026 Torifune flyby outcome
- AstroForge Odin (early failure)

**GPT:**
- OVIRS instrument paper (Reuter et al., Space Science Reviews 2018)
- Lauretta et al., Meteoritics & Planetary Science 2024 (Bennu sample properties)
- Tachibana et al., Science 2022

**Gemini:**
- NEA Scout (contested, §4.2)
- Philae SD2 drill
- The OSIRIS-REx 50 cm sinking figure (flagged as unverified by Claude)

### 4.4 Background items flagged as unverified

- **Claude:** several arXiv IDs in the supplied reviews; the DISCUS NIR spectrometer specification (Claude understood DISCUS as a radar concept); "Ballouz et al. 2020" for TAG bearing capacity.
- **GPT:** declines the supplied resolution and accuracy percentages and the miniaturised-instrument TRLs unless identifiable test reports are provided.

---

## 5. Consolidated development path

Steps are merged where the models describe equivalent work. The source model and its figures are kept for each step. Where models assign different "reaches TRL" values to equivalent steps, both are shown.

| # | Step | Claude | Gemini | GPT | Reaches TRL |
